---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The five lifecycle commands are `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`; `project check` is their read-only pre-finalize source gate and never writes a receipt.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. `workspace` is Domainry's tenant boundary, not a peer of a separate tenant concept: translate tenant wording in requirements to workspace context, and never author a `tenant` or `workspace` Object/table, project-owned `tenant_id`/`workspace_id`, or duplicate workspace identity/projection. A company, customer, merchant, store, or other independently required business aggregate must use its actual domain name and lifecycle, never `tenant` as an infrastructure surrogate. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

When an admitted Project Builder demand declares `project_navigation`, the frontend compiler artifact named there is the complete menu-definition authority. Read it as immutable evidence and never reproduce, summarize, or edit its labels, routes, icons, parentage, or ordering. This backend stage owns only the mapping from published human Role keys to those compiled menu keys; there is one tenant-independent template and no application, client, surface, device, or end dimension.

## model

Select the one task profile and comma-separated requirement topics from the accepted current-batch dependency closure, then request one exact minimum reading plan. Its `capability_contracts` is the complete inlined machine-contract closure for that scope; do not scan the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) or issue one `model capability --key` call per category. Read every returned `read_order` path once, in order, relative to `SKILL_ROOT`. The returned documents, including [backend model](references/backend-model.md) when selected, remain authoritative—the plan removes discovery calls, not semantics. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary human Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants; that shorthand expands to the published `any`/`manual`/workspace-provisioned defaults. In `project.initial_workspace_administrator_role`, explicitly select the one Role assigned to the first Workspace administrator; it must be workspace-provisioned, use `audience:any|user`, use `assignment_mode:manual`, and have no `required_binding_key`. Never infer this selection from a Role suffix, risk level, permissions, ordering, or the first Role. Use an extended Role with `audience: "service"` and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"` for an internal Workflow/Scheduler execution identity, and omit `provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to false; bind that Role by key through Workflow `run_as`, including a Workflow targeted by Scheduler. Never convert an internal role into a human tenant-login actor to satisfy validation.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; inside its SQL, wrap every model-derived Object and field identifier in MySQL backticks even when the key is not a SQL keyword, while keeping aliases, parameter names, and result aliases unquoted. A bounded same-Object aggregate across Runtime-installed Workspaces uses the separate `cross-workspace-aggregate` topic and never caller SQL or Workspace IDs. Use `organization-delivery` for Runtime-selected ownership targets and store provisioning, `identity-handler-delivery` for atomic Identity/Profile delivery, and `workspace-identity-usage` for installation-authorized account counts. Every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --reading-profile <initial-delivery|feature-increment|handler-repair> \
  --topics <records,permissions,identity-profile,identity-handler-delivery,organization,organization-delivery,reporting-line,workflow,scheduler,reports,report-export,cross-workspace-aggregate,workspace-identity-usage,notifications,connectors,agents,entrypoints,workspace-provisioning,files,domain-truth>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. On failure, repair the complete stdout `diagnostics` batch using each file/JSON Pointer, constraint, actual/allowed value and hint before rerunning; its `artifact` path, relative to `--project`, retains the full provenance. Use only the exact contract keys returned in `capability_contracts`; Runtime execution-only modules have none. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Gate on the returned state before reading or writing implementation source. `implementation_ready` or `applied` is materialized success. `evolution_review_required` is an exit-0, non-terminal control state with `materialization_state:not_materialized`: inspect the exact immutable `evolution_audit_path`; verify its raw bytes with `evolution_audit_file_sha256` and `evolution_audit_file_size_bytes`, for example `test "$(shasum -a 256 "$PROJECT_ROOT/$evolution_audit_path" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$evolution_audit_file_sha256" && test "$(wc -c < "$PROJECT_ROOT/$evolution_audit_path" | tr -d '[:space:]')" = "$evolution_audit_file_size_bytes"`; and confirm the JSON document's `audit_sha256` equals `evolution_audit_sha256`. `evolution_audit_sha256_kind:canonical_semantic_identity` means this latter value is the canonical semantic identity computed with the self-hash field empty, not the raw file digest, and it is the value embedded in `next_command`; never compare it to raw `shasum` output. Then rerun the returned `next_command` after replacing its reason placeholder with a non-empty explanation of the reviewed diff. Do not continue to source implementation or finalization until that reapply returns `implementation_ready` or `applied`; repair revalidates the canonical audit content and current inputs, so a tampered or stale audit, omitted SHA/reason, or failed repair remains a non-zero failure. On successful reapply, `evolution_source_finalization.state:deferred_unfinalized_source` means the audit proved the previous delivery had never been finalized: the reviewed in-progress source was preserved, not trusted or finalized, and the ordinary focused-test/`apply finalize` gate remains mandatory. Never delete an existing finalization receipt to force this state; its file SHA is bound into the audit.

If the admitted demand names a compiled navigation artifact, create or update exactly one project-owned `backend/config/navigation-role-menus.json` before finalization. Its only schema is `{"contract_version":"domainry-project-role-menu-sets-v1","role_menu_sets":[{"role_key":"<published-human-role>","menu_keys":["<compiled-menu-key>"]}]}`. Use only workspace-provisioned human Roles from the current model and menu keys present in the compiler artifact. Do not add menu definitions, tenant/workspace IDs, permissions, routes, presentation fields, or client/end selectors. Do not create this file when no compiled navigation artifact exists. Finalization verifies the compiler source digest and menu-key closure and generates the Runtime bootstrap template; Runtime validates the published Role closure, and Identity copies the template into each new Workspace exactly once.

Retain the immutable implementation packet only from a materialized-success response. Read the compact packet index once: its `actions` array is the complete exact Action-context path list, `summary.shared_constraints` applies to every Action, and `summary.test_commands` is the copyable command contract for this delivery. Read its exact `verification.path` core during apply—not after finalization—then read each shard in `verification.minimum_read_plan` exactly once after checking its published byte count and SHA-256; those shards contain only the listed `route_keys` reachable from this project's compiled manifest. Never enumerate or read unlisted route artifacts, and never read the full source route catalog—the core's `route_catalog` identity preserves its completeness. Before authoring any business-flow source, consume `evidence_contract` as the complete marker grammar: use its allowed `source` values and numeric `requirement_id_pattern`, and implement every flow-specific `required_operations` entry with its exact source and `required_observations` (BF08 publishes all seven governed-export steps). Copy `verification.harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go` and author scenarios rather than regenerating transport, authentication, response-decoding, and evidence infrastructure. Consume `setup_contract`, compact `routes`, and the focused shards directly. Build every business-flow precondition for an `action_only` Object through a published authored Action; when a flow needs business actors or organizations, use an authored Identity HandlerDelivery or OrganizationDelivery Action. Bootstrap materializes the Blueprint's eligible human Workspace Roles, assigns only the explicitly selected `initial_workspace_administrator_role` to the first administrator, and keeps service/system-managed Roles out of tenant login provisioning. If the authored Action surface cannot establish an exact required state, repair the Blueprint and Handler contract before finalization, rerun `model plan`, then follow `setup_contract.post_apply_repair`; never inject records, roles, users, organizations, or historical timestamps through a startup fixture. Then read each compact Action context by exact path and follow that context's `read_order` once, in order, relative to `PROJECT_ROOT/backend`; those exact generated contracts and project-owned source/test files replace embedded source dumps and broad generated-tree scans. For this packet, implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests, and create every required `backend/tests/businessflow` case for this batch. Consume every call outcome in Handler and helper source: never use `_` to discard all returns or an error/`ok` result from a capability, method, constructor, parser, or local helper. A data result may be ignored only while its sibling error is bound and handled, such as `_, err := caps.Store.Update(...)`; `value, _ := parse(...)`, `_, _ = call(...)`, and `_ = call(...)` are forbidden. Every multi-item command or query uses one generated batch/bulk capability call; never loop over a single-item capability or Runtime API to simulate batch behavior, including through helper indirection. Pure in-memory loops are allowed only when needed to build bounded batch inputs or correlate results and must contain no capability I/O. If the required true-batch primitive is absent, repair the owning contract instead of hiding the gap with pseudo-batch code; use a bounded sequential fallback only when true batch cannot be implemented and the accepted requirement explicitly defines its non-atomic, partial-failure semantics. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Follow `summary.stage_boundary` literally: finish all project-owned source, then run `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile` before finalization; `focused` runs the Action tests and then `project check`, the exact read-only project-source validation also used by finalization. Treat either part as the same focused gate and repair every emitted diagnostic before advancing. A full-tree failure caused by not-yet-generated composition is not an implementation failure. The shared harness is a template copied into project-owned tests, never imported from `.domainry`. After both pre-finalize commands pass run `summary.test_commands.finalize`, then and only then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. These commands already contain the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, and project-local-plus-public hybrid `GOPROXY`; do not replace them with a default or local-only proxy. Once finalization succeeds, project-owned source is frozen for this verification attempt. Any later source change starts a new repair iteration and requires the focused/compile/finalize sequence again; do not continue the stale attempt into `verify`.

Finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including consumed call outcomes, guarded `ConditionalUpdate`, and the no-pseudo-batch invariant across capability aliases, callbacks, and named local helper call chains. `project check` calls that exact validation without resolving finalization dependencies or writing a receipt; use only the packet-provided command and do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). The implementation packet's verification guide and every required business-flow test must already have been consumed/completed during apply. Verify is read-and-run only: do not create, edit, rename, or delete project-owned source after finalization. Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. For every module HTTP step, resolve the exact route in the implementation packet and grant that route's `authorization.permission` with its `required_role_grant.data_scope` to the selected actor Role before finalization; Report audience/source data access never substitutes for the executable route Permission. Decode Runtime record pages only as top-level `items`, with business fields in each `items[].data` and record metadata such as `id`/`updated_at` on the item envelope. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` reuses structural/package receipts only after their complete source, model, Runtime and dependency identities validate; otherwise it runs the complete backend tree and rebuilds. It always proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves Runtime stopped and emits stage/cache telemetry. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. For both phases every BF01-BF08 test emits its structured evidence marker exactly as verification documents. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a project evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.

| BF04 / `TestBF04ApprovalRejectedReasonAndNotification` in `backend/tests/businessflow/bf04_test.go` | owner rep + director | own qualified high amount | start Workflow and reject(reason) | qualified, rejection reason, notification, zero customer | unauthorized/replay no extra notification/customer | restart reads rejected facts |
| BF05 / `TestBF05DepartmentScopePaginationAndEntrypoints` in `backend/tests/businessflow/bf05_test.go` | east/north reps + director exact org | >=6 records across org/status/amount | bounded pages + entrypoint projection | same-dept and director counts/menus exact | cross-dept target absent | restart same visibility |
| BF06 / `TestBF06WeekdayReminderDedupAndRestart` in `backend/tests/businessflow/bf06_test.go` | service scheduler + stale lead owner | contacted lead with Action-supported historical timestamp/precondition | trigger/observe worker and inbox | one reminder with lead/date | same-day rerun count unchanged | phase 2 same reminder durable |
